script: [serious] Hours before the Deepwater Horizon exploded, a test told the crew the well was leaking. They decided it was fine. April twentieth, twenty ten. A drilling rig in the Gulf of Mexico was sealing a deep oil well with cement, to come back for it later. Before leaving, the crew ran a safety check, called a negative pressure test. If the cement held, the pressure should stay at zero. It didn't. The readings showed pressure building, a sign that oil and gas were seeping into the well. The supervisors accepted an explanation that later investigators called facially implausible, and declared the test a success. No one called an engineer on shore for a second opinion. That evening, warning signs kept coming. At nine forty-nine p.m., mud and gas burst onto the rig floor. Then it exploded. Eleven workers were killed. The oil flowed into the Gulf for eighty-seven days. The presidential commission called the test a major contributing factor. Send this to someone who says the numbers are probably fine. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number fifty-five. A new file every day.
